picks.reason: The hypotheses use terms (more satisfying, traditional voice automation, hang up immediately, immediately ask for a human) that need fixed working definitions before any quote can count for or against them.
Each hypothesis is a broad claim. Splitting it into sub-claims that must all hold shows which quote bears on which part.
A participant by hypothesis matrix gives a visible base for reading across the eight participants and shows where they disagree.
Rating each quote against rival readings of each hypothesis shows which quotes discriminate and which fit every reading. It reaches the associate level.
Treating each participant as a case with the same questions shows consistent patterns and deviant cases for each hypothesis.
The material quotes only some participants and some scenarios. This separates silence from evidence against.
All quotes come from one source (one study, one prompt set). This shows which findings rest on a single voice and what is missing.
A deliberate search for statements that contradict each hypothesis tests the readings that look supported.
Every quote the analyses use must be confirmed by string match to exist in the source.
Re-running the verdicts after dropping single participants or changing a definition shows whether a verdict reverses on eight people.
A bias check guards against confirmation of the stated hypotheses and over-weighting of vivid quotes.
A second person who did not build the analysis should review the verdicts and be able to overrule them.

gaps: No listed technique supplies a statistical test of association, which ten quotes from eight participants could not support. The associate claim therefore reads as patterns within this sample only.
